blocks.prompt: 15. If the arithmetic progressions \(3, 10, 17, \ldots\) and \(63, 65, 67, \ldots\) are such that their \(n^{\text{th}}\) terms are equal, then find the value of \(n\).
blocks.explanation:
Two different A.P.s; at one position \(n\) their terms are the same.
We must find that \(n\).
Plan: write the \(n\)th term of each, set them equal and solve.
steps:
Given: A.P. 1: \(3, 10, 17, \ldots\); A.P. 2: \(63, 65, 67, \ldots\)
To find: \(n\) with equal \(n\)th terms.
Method: \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) for each, then one linear equation.

nth term of the first A.P.
\[a_1 = 3,\quad d = 7\]
\[a_n = 3 + (n - 1)7 = 7n - 4\]
Why: \(10 - 3 = 7\).

nth term of the second A.P.
\[b_1 = 63,\quad d' = 2\]
\[b_n = 63 + (n - 1)2 = 2n + 61\]
Why: \(65 - 63 = 2\).

Set them equal and solve
\[7n - 4 = 2n + 61\]
\[5n = 65\]
\[n = 13\]
Why: The first A.P. grows faster (7 per step against 2), so it catches up with the second at one position.
